# Automating Flashback exports (v0.39.10, MC 1.21.11, Fabric)

Goal: after a session, no human touches the game: a script reads the replay, writes camera moves, a render runs, and B-roll mp4 files appear.
Facts below are read from the decompiled source (`tools/flashback_src/`); "inferred" marks what could not be run. Nothing here was run in-game.

## 1. What the export does

`File > Export Video` -> `StartExportWindow.open()` -> modal `###StartExport` -> button *Start Export* ->
`createExportSettings()` -> **native NFD save dialog** (`AsyncFileDialogs.saveFileDialog`, Win32 common dialog; folder dialog for PNG sequence)
-> `new ExportSettings(...)` -> `Flashback.EXPORT_JOB = new ExportJob(settings)` (static field).

`ExportSettings` is a plain record: `name, EditorState (a copy), initialCameraPosition/Yaw/Pitch (from the local replay-camera player),
resolutionX/Y, startTick, endTick, framerate, resetRng, container, codec, encoder, bitrate, transparent, ssaa, noGui, recordAudio,
stereoAudio, audioCodec, output Path, pngSequenceFormat`. Values come from `config.internalExport` (persisted in
`config/flashback/flashback.json`) except bitrate (static text field, default `20m`) and the output path (dialog).
Start/end = scene `exportStartTicks/EndTicks`, else first/last keyframe, else whole replay.

`MixinMinecraft.runTick_runAllTasks` (every client frame): if `ExportJobQueue.drainingQueue` and no job, pops the next queued
`ExportSettings`; if `EXPORT_JOB != null && !ReplayUI.isActive()` it calls `ExportJob.run()` **synchronously on the render thread**
(`PerfectFrames.enable()` first), then sets `EXPORT_JOB = null`. So an export needs: a running `ReplayServer`
(`Flashback.getReplayServer()`, created by `Flashback.openReplayWorld(Path)`), the local player/level, a GL window, and an `EditorState`
(loaded from `flashback/editor_states/<replay uuid>.json`). The ImGui editor itself is *not* required: `isActiveInternal()` returns false while a job exists.

`ExportJob.run()`: `doExport` -> `setup()` (seek to start-40, tick forward, apply keyframes at start) -> `calculateTicks()` (one `TickInfo` per output
frame; speed/timelapse/freeze keyframes change ticks per frame) -> per frame: `setServerTickAndWait` (replay server goes to the tick),
client ticks, `applyKeyframes` (camera etc.), 60 dummy warm-up frames on the first frame, render at the ExportJob resolution (the window
framebuffer size is overridden by `MixinWindow`), async GPU read-back (`SaveableFramebufferQueue`, 3 deep) -> `VideoWriter.encode`.
`AsyncFFmpegVideoWriter` uses bytedeco FFmpeg (bundled in the 210 MB jar) with two worker threads (rescale + encode) and writes to
`replay_export_temp/<uuid>.<ext>` (relative to the game dir), then moves the file to `settings.output()` on success
(`ExportDoneWindow` entry). `ExportJobQueue.queuedJobs` is an in-memory static list (not persisted); *Start All* sets `drainingQueue`.
Cancel = hold ESC 3 s. Fullscreen blocks the Start button (dialog text `export_disable_fullscreen`).

## 2. Ways to trigger exports, ranked

### Rank 1: tiny Fabric mod "flashback_auto" (recommended)
Everything needed is public static state in Flashback:
1. `Minecraft.execute(() -> Flashback.openReplayWorld(Path zip))` (public static; also registers recent replay; loads our editor-state file).
2. Poll until `Flashback.getReplayServer() != null && mc.player != null && mc.level != null && mc.screen == null` (+ ~1 s).
3. Per job: `EditorState es = EditorStateManager.getCurrent(); long s = es.acquireWrite(); es.setSceneIndex(i, s); es.release(s);`
   then `new ExportSettings(name, es.copy(), player.position(), yRot, xRot, w, h, start, end, fps, resetRng, VideoContainer, VideoCodec, encoder,
   bitrate, transparent, ssaa, noGui, recordAudio, stereo, audioCodec, outputPath, "%04d")`; `encoder` = `codec.getEncoders()[0]` or a choice.
4. `Flashback.EXPORT_JOB = new ExportJob(settings)`; the mixin runs it next frame; wait until `EXPORT_JOB == null`; verify the output file.
5. Next job / next replay / `Minecraft.stop()`.
Hooks available to piggy-back: no Flashback API, events or export commands. Only client commands `/flashback start|finish|pause|unpause|config|mark`
(+ `/hide`, `/show` inside a replay). Mixins are not needed.

Toolchain (nothing installed or downloaded by this research):
* **Compile without Gradle/Loom**: the Minecraft runtime already on the machine (`.minecraft/runtime/java-runtime-delta`, OpenJDK 21.0.7) contains
  the `jdk.compiler` and `jdk.jartool` modules (checked with `java --list-modules`), so `java -m jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.Main` and
  `java -m jdk.jartool/sun.tools.jar.Main` work without a JDK download (inferred: compiler not actually invoked, see section 5).
* Class path (all local): `.minecraft/.fabric/remappedJars/minecraft-1.21.11-0.19.2/client-intermediary.jar` (32 MB), the Flashback jar,
  `libraries/net/fabricmc/fabric-loader/0.19.2/fabric-loader-0.19.2.jar`, gson, joml, guava, authlib, DFU, brigadier, fastutil, netty-buffer.
  Because Fabric runs the game with **intermediary** names, source written with `class_310`/`class_243`/`class_746`/`method_1551()`/`method_20493()` needs no
  remapping (names to use are in `flashback_src`, e.g. `StartExportWindow`: `player.method_73189()`, `method_36454()`, `method_36455()`).
  The mod is ~150 lines, a `fabric.mod.json` and a client entrypoint; a poll thread posts `Minecraft.execute` every 250 ms (no Fabric API needed).
* The standard route, if the creator prefers readable names: JDK 21 (~190 MB zip, e.g. Microsoft/Temurin), Gradle wrapper (~135 MB, auto-downloaded),
  Fabric Loom plugin, `loom.officialMojangMappings()` (Flashback itself is written against Mojang names), `modCompileOnly files(<Flashback jar>)`
  (Loom remaps the 210 MB jar intermediary -> named, one-off, several hundred MB of cache), MC client+server jars (~60-100 MB), libraries (~150 MB).
  URLs: gradle.org/releases, fabricmc.net/develop (template generator), adoptium.net / learn.microsoft.com/java/openjdk. **Needs creator approval.**
* Risks: reaches into Flashback internals (`ExportSettings` constructor order changes between versions: pin to 0.39.10, re-check on update);

class Target:
    """Anything with ``pos(tick)->(x,y,z)`` feet position and ``rot(tick)->(yaw,pitch)``;
    ``flashback_replay.Track`` satisfies this. ``uuid`` is needed only for track_follow."""

    def __init__(self, pos: Callable[[int], tuple], rot: Callable[[int], tuple] | None = None,
                 uuid: str | None = None, name: str = "target"):
        self.pos = pos
        self.rot = rot or (lambda t: (0.0, 0.0))
        self.uuid = uuid
        self.name = name


def as_target(obj, uuid: str | None = None) -> Target:
    if isinstance(obj, Target):
        return obj
    return Target(obj.pos, obj.rot, uuid or getattr(obj, "key", None), getattr(obj, "name", None) or "target")


def _ease(kind: str):

def orbit(target, start: int, seconds: float = 6.0, radius: float = 6.0, height: float = 2.0,
          revolutions: float = 1.0, direction: int = 1, start_angle: float | None = None,
          center_offset=(0.0, 1.2, 0.0), ease: str = "inout", samples_per_s: float = 4.0,
          name: str | None = None) -> Shot:
    """Camera circles the (moving) target, always looking at it. One CAMERA_ORBIT track.

    radius = horizontal distance, height = camera height above the look-at point.
    ``start_angle`` = camera look yaw at the start (default: target's facing -> camera behind it).
    direction +1 = clockwise seen from above. Yaw is NOT wrapped (orbit interpolation is plain linear/CatmullRom
    on the number, so 360*n works)."""
    tg = as_target(target)
    ticks, total = _ticks(start, seconds, samples_per_s)
    e = _ease(ease)
    d = math.hypot(radius, height)
    pitch = math.degrees(math.atan2(height, radius))
    y0 = tg.rot(start)[0] if start_angle is None else start_angle
    kfs = {}
    n = len(ticks) - 1
    for i, t in enumerate(ticks):
        u = e(i / n)
        px, py, pz = tg.pos(t)
        c = (px + center_offset[0], py + center_offset[1], pz + center_offset[2])
        kfs[t] = orbit_kf(c, d, y0 + direction * 360.0 * revolutions * u, pitch)
    return Shot(name or f"orbit@{start}", "orbit", start, ticks[-1], [Track("CAMERA_ORBIT", kfs)],
                f"orbit r={radius} h={height} rev={revolutions}", dict(radius=radius, height=height))


def drone_pullup(target, start: int, seconds: float = 5.0, start_dist: float = 3.5, end_dist: float = 45.0,
                 start_pitch: float = 8.0, end_pitch: float = 68.0, yaw_drift: float = 35.0,
                 start_angle: float | None = None, center_offset=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), ease: str = "inout",
                 samples_per_s: float = 5.0, name: str | None = None) -> Shot:
    """Camera starts low and close behind the target and rises/backs away while tilting down (reveal shot)."""
    tg = as_target(target)
    ticks, total = _ticks(start, seconds, samples_per_s)
    e = _ease(ease)
    y0 = tg.rot(start)[0] if start_angle is None else start_angle
    n = len(ticks) - 1
    kfs = {}
    for i, t in enumerate(ticks):
        u = e(i / n)
        px, py, pz = tg.pos(t)
        c = (px + center_offset[0], py + center_offset[1], pz + center_offset[2])
        dist = start_dist * (end_dist / start_dist) ** u          # exponential => constant perceived speed
        kfs[t] = orbit_kf(c, dist, y0 + yaw_drift * u, _lerp(start_pitch, end_pitch, u))
    return Shot(name or f"drone_pullup@{start}", "drone_pullup", start, ticks[-1], [Track("CAMERA_ORBIT", kfs)],

DEFAULT_SHOT_SECONDS = {"orbit": 6.0, "drone_pullup": 5.0, "push_in": 3.5, "flyby": 4.5, "track_follow": 6.0}


def auto_shots(replay, max_shots: int = 8, seconds_scale: float = 1.0, lead_s: float = 1.0) -> list[Shot]:
    """Turn ``replay.suggest_moments()`` into Shot objects around the recording player."""
    from .flashback_replay import Replay  # local import to keep modules decoupled

    assert isinstance(replay, Replay)
    tg = as_target(replay.player_track(), replay.local_uuid)
    shots: list[Shot] = []
    for m in replay.suggest_moments(top=max_shots * 2):
        kind = m["suggested_shot"]
        secs = DEFAULT_SHOT_SECONDS.get(kind, 5.0) * seconds_scale
        start = max(0, int(m["tick"] - lead_s * 20))
        end_cap = replay.total_ticks - 2
        if start + int(secs * 20) > end_cap:
            start = max(0, end_cap - int(secs * 20))
        tag = f"{m['kind']}@{m['tick']}"
        if kind == "orbit":
            s = orbit(tg, start, secs, name=tag)
        elif kind == "drone_pullup":
            s = drone_pullup(tg, start, secs, name=tag)
        elif kind == "push_in":
            s = push_in(tg, start, secs, name=tag)
        elif kind == "flyby":
            s = flyby(tg, start, secs, name=tag)
        elif kind == "track_follow":
            s = track_follow(tg, start, secs, name=tag)
        else:
            continue
        s.note = m["reason"]
        shots.append(s)
        if len(shots) >= max_shots:
            break
    return shots


@dataclass
class ExportOptions:
    """Per-job export settings consumed by the flashback_auto mod (maps 1:1 onto ExportSettings)."""

    width: int = 1920
    height: int = 1080
    fps: float = 60.0
    container: str = "MP4"
    codec: str = "H264"
    encoder: str | None = None        # e.g. "libx264", "h264_amf" (None -> Flashback's first valid encoder)
    bitrate: int = 20_000_000
    ssaa: bool = False
    no_gui: bool = True
    reset_rng: bool = False
    record_audio: bool = False
    transparent: bool = False


def jobs_json(replay_path: str | Path, shots: Sequence[Shot], out_dir: str | Path,
              opts: ExportOptions | None = None, prefix: str = "") -> dict:
    """Job list for the flashback_auto mod: one job per scene/shot, rendered to <out_dir>/<prefix><shot>.mp4."""
    opts = opts or ExportOptions()
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    jobs = []
    for i, s in enumerate(shots):
        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+", "_", f"{prefix}{i:02d}_{s.name}")
        jobs.append({
            "scene": i, "name": safe, "start": s.start, "end": s.end,
            "output": str(out_dir / f"{safe}.{opts.container.lower() if opts.container != 'PNG_SEQUENCE' else 'png'}"),
            "width": opts.width, "height": opts.height, "fps": opts.fps, "container": opts.container,
            "codec": opts.codec, "encoder": opts.encoder, "bitrate": opts.bitrate, "ssaa": opts.ssaa,
            "noGui": opts.no_gui, "resetRng": opts.reset_rng, "recordAudio": opts.record_audio,
            "transparent": opts.transparent, "kind": s.kind, "note": s.note,
        })
    return {"version": 1, "replay": str(replay_path), "jobs": jobs}

def default_visuals() -> dict:
    return {k: copy.deepcopy(v[1]) for k, v in VISUALS_FIELDS.items()}


@dataclass
class Visuals:
    """High level visual overrides applied to the whole editor state (``replayVisuals``)."""

    hide_nametags: bool = True
    hide_hud: bool = True           # chat/boss bar/title/scoreboard/action bar/hotbar off
    night_vision: bool = False
    time_of_day: int | None = None  # 0..24000 (6000 = noon, 18000 = midnight); None = leave replay time
    weather: str = "NONE"
    fov: float | None = None        # global override (degrees); None = keep the in-game FOV
    camera_path_overlay: bool = False  # the editor's camera-path gizmo (never wanted in a render)
    render_particles: bool = True
    aspect: str | None = None       # e.g. "ASPECT_9_16" for shorts -> sizing CHANGE_ASPECT_RATIO
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # raw replayVisuals overrides

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        d = default_visuals()
        if self.hide_nametags:
            d["renderNametags"] = False
        if self.hide_hud:
            for k in ("showChat", "showBossBar", "showTitleText", "showScoreboard", "showActionBar", "showHotbar"):
                d[k] = False
        d["overrideNightVision"] = bool(self.night_vision)
        if self.time_of_day is not None:
            d["overrideTimeOfDay"] = int(self.time_of_day)
        d["overrideWeatherMode"] = self.weather
        if self.fov is not None:
            d["overrideFov"] = True
            d["overrideFovAmount"] = float(self.fov)
        d["cameraPath"] = bool(self.camera_path_overlay)
        d["renderParticles"] = bool(self.render_particles)
        if self.aspect:
            d["sizing"] = "CHANGE_ASPECT_RATIO"
            d["changeAspectRatio"] = self.aspect
        d.update(self.extra)
        return d

def dumps_state(state: dict) -> str:
    """Compact JSON like ``FlashbackGson.COMPRESSED`` (no spaces, doubles keep '.0')."""
    return json.dumps(state, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def write_state(state: dict, replay_uuid: str, folder: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Write ``<folder>/<replay_uuid>.json``. ``folder`` must be ``<.minecraft>/flashback/editor_states``
    for Flashback to pick it up -- this function does not default to it on purpose.
    The previous file (if any) is kept as ``.json.old`` exactly like EditorStateManager.save() does."""
    errs = validate_state(state)
    if errs:
        raise ValueError("invalid editor state:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errs))
    folder = Path(folder)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p = folder / f"{replay_uuid}.json"
    if p.exists():
        p.replace(folder / f"{replay_uuid}.json.old")
    p.write_text(dumps_state(state), encoding="utf-8")
    return p

# Cinematic Director (replay B-roll)

You play normally while Flashback (and Replay Mod) record. Afterwards the editor works out where a cinematic shot helps the
video (an establishing aerial, an orbit after loot, a pull-back before a death, a chase cam in a panic...), asks the replay
for that shot, checks the clip, and lays it over the gameplay **while your voice keeps going**. The video never gets longer.

Code: `mcstudio/cinematic.py`. Tests: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe tests/test_cinematic.py` (or `mcs cinematic selftest`).

## The flow

```
OBS video + Flashback replay
  1 find_replay      pick the replay that overlaps the recording in wall-clock time
  2 sync             replay time at video t=0:  timestamps, then refined by motion cross-correlation
  3 plan_shots       choose shots from transcript beats, death screens, dark/calm stretches, replay events
                     -> projects/<slug>/broll/shots.json
  4 queue_jobs       studio/cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json   (one per shot, with a Flashback editor state)
  5 exporter         fake | manual | flashback_auto  -> projects/<slug>/broll/<shot>.mp4
  6 qa_clip          reject black / frozen / blurred / inside-a-block / wrong-format clips (kept on disk, reason recorded)
  7 splice_into_edl  full-frame muted video overlays + a soft whoosh, only for rendered + QA-passed shots
```

CLI (run from `studio/`): `uv run mcs cinematic plan <slug>` (add `--synthetic` for a dry run without a replay),
`render <slug> [--exporter fake|manual|flashback_auto] [--force]`, `status <slug>`, `splice <slug>`
(writes `edit.json`, backup `edit.v_precinematic.json`), `qa <file> [--project slug]`, `sync <slug>`.

## Sync (how a shot finds its moment in the replay)

* OBS filename `YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS` is the recording start (whole seconds). It is refined to ~0.1 s with
  file end time minus the longest stream duration (real session: 36.92 s vs the OBS log's 36.83 s).
* Flashback `metadata.json` `name` is the **save time**, so start = name - total_ticks/20 (checked on the real files: the zip is
  written 2-5 s after `name`, and the Replay Mod recording of the same session ends within seconds of it).
* Replay Mod `metaData.json` `date` (epoch ms) is the **start**; `duration` is in ms.
* `estimate_sync` = video start - replay start (good to a second or two). `refine_sync` correlates the video's motion energy
  (ffmpeg, 4 fps, 64x36) with the replay player's speed + yaw rate + pitch rate over +-15 s and reports a confidence; below
  `sync_min_confidence` (0.4) it keeps the timestamp offset and says so.
* Measured on the real 15:02 session (94.5 s video): timestamps 22.6 s (filename only) / 23.5 s (refined start), motion
  cross-correlation 23.37 s, confidence 0.90. Run at 12 fps: 23.44 s overall, 23.47 s from the first half of the video and 23.41 s
  from the second half (independent estimates agree within 0.06 s, so no clock drift). The OBS log gives 23.43 s.

## Director rules (all configurable, see Settings > Cinematic shots)

* Plans on the **timeline the viewer sees**: output time when `edit.json` exists, else source time. A shot may run across a jump cut.
* 2.5-5 s per shot; at least `min_gap_s` (20) of normal footage between shots; at most `max_shots_per_min` (3) scaled by length
  (at least 1 for videos over 40 s); never the same kind back to back; first `hook_s` (8) seconds untouched.
* Never on a punchline word (beats of score 3+), a running-gag counter, a death screen, or an existing meme cutaway /
  green screen / sticker. Shots start just after the line lands.
* Intro `aerial_establish` at the first calm moment; loot/victory -> `orbit`/`push_in`; death -> `death_reveal` that **ends**
  just before the death screen; panic -> `track_follow`/`pov`; location/dimension -> `nether_arrival`; calm stretches ->
  `flyby`/`timelapse` (dark footage preferred); outro line -> `outro_pullup` (golden hour via time override for night sessions).
* When no window is free the shot is skipped and listed under `skipped` with the reason. A dense edit (lots of memes, counters and
  cuts) gets few shots: that is intended.
* Replay events (death, dimension, explosion, kill) are only trusted when sync confidence >= `trust_replay_events` (0.5).

## Contract: `projects/<slug>/broll/shots.json`

```jsonc
{"project": "ep01", "replay": "<zip>", "replay_kind": "flashback|replaymod|synthetic", "timeline": "output|source",
 "sync": {"offset_s": 23.37, "method": "timestamps|motion-xcorr|event", "confidence": 0.9, "notes": "..."},
 "settings": {"...snapshot of the cinematic settings..."},
 "notes": [], "skipped": [{"kind": "...", "reason": "...", "why": "..."}],
 "shots": [{
   "id": "shot-01", "kind": "aerial_establish|orbit|drone_pullup|push_in|flyby|track_follow|pov|spectate|timelapse|nether_arrival|death_reveal|outro_pullup",
   "moment": "intro|loot|death|panic|victory|travel|build|new_place|outro", "reason": "...",
   "video_t": 26.71,      // SOURCE second where the shot starts   (replay_tick = (video_t + offset_s) * 20)
   "out_t": 20.0,         // second on the planning timeline (output time when the plan was made from an edit)
   "replay_tick": 734, "ticks": 63, "dur_s": 3.15,
   "params": {"camera": {...abstract recipe...}, "anchor": {"tick","x","y","z","yaw","pitch"}|null,
              "visuals": {"hide_gui","hide_nametags","hide_chat","night_vision","time_of_day"}, "fps": 30},
   "status": "planned|queued|rendered|rejected|failed", "file": "broll/shot-01.mp4"|null, "qa": {...}|null}]}
```

Job file (`cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json`): replay path, `tick_start/tick_end/ticks`, `anchor`, `camera.abstract`,
`camera.keyframes` (a validated Flashback editor state from `flashback_keyframes`, null if there is no replay), `visuals`,
`export` (1920x1080, fps 30 or 60 for POV, h264, `output` relative + `output_abs`).

## Splice

Each rendered, QA-passed shot becomes `{"type":"video","file":"broll/shot-01.mp4","placement":"fullscreen","audio":false,
"seg":<segment>,"src_at":<video_t>,"dur":<dur_s>,"cinematic":"shot-01"}` placed **under** stickers and motion graphics
(captions and text are drawn after overlays, so they stay readable), plus a quiet `whoosh` SFX (role `whoosh`, -2 dB nudge on
top of the automatic voice-relative level). Re-running removes and re-adds the cinematic items. Shots are dropped, not moved, if
they now overlap a meme/green screen/sticker, sit in the hook, or lose their footage. Vertical shorts leave the B-roll out.
`splice_into_edl(edl, slug)` is the pure function the autopilot calls.

## Real vs stubbed

| Piece | Status |
|---|---|
| Timestamp parsing, replay lookup, sync math, motion cross-correlation | real, verified on the real replays and a real OBS+Flashback session |
| Director, jobs, QA, splice, settings, CLI | real |
| Flashback editor states / keyframes | real (from `flashback_keyframes`, validated, not yet opened in the game) |
| `FakeExporter` | real: labelled placeholder clips for testing the pipeline |
| `ManualExporter` | real: writes `CHECKLIST.md`; export by hand into the given file, then run `render` again to QA it |
| `FlashbackAutoExporter` | **stub** (raises with a pointer to `docs/flashback-automation.md`) |
| Replay Mod `.mcpr` shots | windows/sync only; no reader, so no shots from `.mcpr` yet |
| Real shots in a real edit | not validated: needs the exporter plus a real OBS+Flashback session end to end |

The Cinematic Director is built and its 12 tests pass, including sync on the real 15:02 OBS+Flashback session. It is not validated end to end with real shots, because the hands-off exporter does not exist yet.

## Sync accuracy on the real 15:02 session
- **Result:** motion cross-correlation (the video's motion energy against the replay player's speed and turning) gives replay time at video t=0 of **23.37 s**, confidence **0.90** (peak r 0.65, rival peak 0.32).
- **Agreement:** the OBS log implies 23.43 s, so the error is about 0.06 s.
- **Other estimates:** timestamps from the OBS filename alone give 22.6 s, which is 0.8 s off. With the start refined from file end time minus duration they give 23.5 s.
- **12 fps run, no drift:** 23.44 s overall. The first half of the video gives 23.47 s and the second half 23.41 s, so the two halves agree within 0.06 s. The Replay Mod pair (26.1 s timestamp estimate) is not used for shots.
- **Not checked:** I did not verify against the "three jumps" markers. The video's motion peaks near the jumps were ambiguous at 4 fps, so the OBS log is the only ground truth used.
- **Cost:** the motion series takes about 25–30 s of CPU for a 95 s 1080p60 clip.

## Timestamp math, verified on the real files
- Flashback `metadata.json` `name` is the save time, so replay start = name − total_ticks/20. The zip is written 2–5 s after `name`.
- Replay Mod `metaData.json` `date` is the start in epoch ms, and `duration` is in ms.
- Flashback and Replay Mod recordings of the same session overlap correctly, and the two sessions do not cross-match.

## Files
- `studio/mcstudio/cinematic.py` — the module.
  - It exposes `find_replay`, `estimate_sync`, `refine_sync`, `plan_shots`, `queue_jobs`, `render_queue`, `qa_clip`, `splice`, and `splice_into_edl(edl, slug)`.
  - It also holds the exporter classes `FakeExporter`, `ManualExporter` and `FlashbackAutoExporter`, plus a synthetic replay for dry runs.
- `studio/tests/test_cinematic.py` — run it with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe tests/test_cinematic.py` or `mcs cinematic selftest`.
- `studio/docs/cinematic-pipeline.md` — plain-language overview, the `shots.json` contract, and what is real versus stubbed.
- Small edits to other files, each marked `# [cinematic]`:
  - `settings.py`: a `cinematic` section.
  - `cli.py`: `mcs cinematic ...` (`mcs cinematic -h` is swallowed by the passthrough; `mcs cinematic plan -h` works).
  - `shorts.py`: shorts drop cinematic overlays and their whoosh. Render stretches a fullscreen 16:9 clip into 9:16, so this is needed. It is a small edit outside what you listed, so revert it if you disagree.
- I did not touch `autoplan.py`, `pipeline.py`, `server.py` or `ui/*`.
- `test_autopilot.py` still passes.

## Contract
- `shots.json` follows your schema.
- Two additions per shot:
  - `out_t`, the second on the planning timeline.
  - `timeline`, at the top level: "output" or "source".
- `video_t` is the source second and `replay_tick = (video_t + offset) * 20`.
- The plan also records `skipped` shots with reasons.
- Each job file carries a validated Flashback editor state under `camera.keyframes`. It is built with `flashback_keyframes`: all 12 shot kinds validate on the synthetic track and the real replay.

## Director behaviour
- **Timeline:** it plans in output time when `edit.json` exists, so a shot may run across a jump cut. It plans in source time otherwise.
- **Placement rules:**
  - Shots are 2.5–5 s.
  - There is at least 20 s between shots.
  - The first 8 s stay untouched.
  - Shots never land on a punchline beat, a running-gag counter, a death screen, or an existing meme, green screen or sticker.
  - The same kind never repeats back to back.
  - Replay events are only trusted at sync confidence of 0.5 or higher.
- **Splice:**
  - It adds muted fullscreen `video` overlays, placed under stickers and motion graphics.
  - It adds a quiet whoosh at -2 dB.
  - It is idempotent.
  - It returns the edl unchanged if there are no rendered shots or the section is disabled.
  - Captions are drawn after overlays, so they stay readable.

## End-to-end result
- I ran this on a scratch copy of `auto-dig` with a synthetic replay: plan, queue, fake exporter, QA, splice, then `render --preview`. I extracted frames at each shot.
- The placeholder clips replaced the picture and the captions kept advancing on top. The timelapse started right after "NOW WE MAKE... MORE STUFF WITH", with no punchline covered.
- Render shifts shots about 1 s later than the plan because its cut guard lengthens segment boundaries (105.7 s output vs 104 s planned). The overlays are anchored by segment, so they follow.
- The dense real `auto-dig` edit yields only 2 shots: an aerial at 20 s output and a timelapse at 64.8 s or a push-in at 75.6 s, depending on whether the memes are in the edit.

| shot | video_t | out_t | kind | reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | 26.7 | 20.0 | aerial_establish | first calm moment after the hook |
| 02 | 77.9 | 64.8 | timelapse | calm 24 s stretch, dark footage (no memes in the edit) |
| 02 | 90.8 | 75.6 | push_in | replay explosion (edit with memes) |

- The death reveal and the panic chase cam were skipped. The 1.1 s free window before the death screen is too short, and the green screen already sits there.
- Fewer shots in a dense edit is intended, and the plan lists why each one was skipped.
- The scratch projects and job folders are removed. `auto-dig` and all other projects are untouched.
